audit_findings.title: The current denominator may receive post-FY2025 buyback benefits without the associated financing cost in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 6.564806 million shares repurchased for $473.2 million in H1 2026; debt increased $340.220 million; the 50.645582 million valuation denominator is 8.1% below the 55.113645 million February 2026 share count and raises per-share value by 8.8% before financing effects (base $35.95 versus $33.02)
audit_findings.mechanism: The lower share denominator increases value per share, while equity-level OE ending in FY2025 does not include a full period of interest on the June 2026 debt used alongside cash to fund repurchases.
audit_findings.evidence: As of February 13, 2026, there were 55,113,645 shares of the registrant’s common stock outstanding.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated: substantial repurchases and higher debt occurred after the OE history ended. The exact portion of borrowing attributable to repurchases and its normalized after-tax interest cost remain unresolved, but the documented 8.8% denominator uplift alone is large enough to affect the valuation materially.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each post-FY2025 retirement to cash, operating cash flow and borrowing sources; calculate full-period after-tax interest on the resulting capital structure; rerun all scenarios with matched OE and fully diluted shares.

audit_findings.title: Expiring interest-rate protection may make historical equity OE an invalid forward run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,287.386 million June 2026 debt; $400 million of listed caps expire October 31, 2026, after which only $300 million remains capped through October 31, 2027, leaving up to $987.386 million outside the listed caps if debt is unchanged; exact OE impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher after-tax interest expense reduces equity-level OE because interest remains in the numerator; mechanically growing historical OE would omit that prospective burden.
audit_findings.evidence: While we have entered into interest rate cap agreements to limit our exposure to higher interest rates on a portion of our debt, these agreements have expiration dates in 2026 and 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: Partial coverage and near-term cap expirations are demonstrated, while future rates, debt balances and replacement hedges are unresolved. Relative to the $117.9 million OE anchor, exposure approaching $1.0 billion is reasonably capable of materially changing normalized OE and the scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Build a currency-specific debt and after-tax interest schedule using contractual spreads, projected benchmark rates, cap notionals and expiration dates; normalize the OE anchor and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may include captive assets that are not available to common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $0 of the $39.5 million captive debt securities is included in the $163.691 million bridge; the securities are classified as $13.4 million of prepaid/current assets and $26.1 million of other assets, while the bridge equals the separately reported cash-and-cash-equivalents balance
audit_findings.mechanism: The alleged overstatement would enter through the surplus-cash bridge, but the identified captive securities are outside that bridge amount.
audit_findings.evidence: These securities are held in escrow by the Company’s wholly-owned captive insurance company and were purchased with restricted cash.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed balance-sheet trace resolves this specific concern. The valuation adds the $163.691 million cash-and-cash-equivalents line, not the $39.5 million escrowed captive investment portfolio; restricted cash is also reported separately. Consequently, the identified captive securities contribute no value to the bridge.
audit_findings.action: Retain the balance-sheet trace in the valuation record; no rerun is needed for the identified captive securities unless a later filing shows captive or restricted amounts inside cash and cash equivalents.

audit_findings.title: The trend anchor may retain temporary pandemic assistance
audit_findings.magnitude: $31.9 million net pre-tax 2023 benefit from the $49.4 million cost reduction less the $17.5 million reduction in employer subsidies; approximately $19.8 million after tax at the filed 38.0% 2023 effective rate, equal to 17.7% of 2023 OE of $111.9 million
audit_findings.mechanism: If not reversed, temporary assistance inflates 2023 OE and therefore the ten-year log-trend used to set the $117.9 million anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2023, funding received from pandemic-related government support programs reduced center cost of services by $ 49.4 million, of which $ 17.5 million reduced the operating subsidies paid by employers for the related child care centers.
audit_findings.explanation: The temporary benefit in the filed 2023 results is demonstrated, but the record does not establish whether the OE calculation already removed it. Its possible after-tax contamination is substantial relative to both 2023 OE and the selected anchor, so it is reasonably capable of changing the scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the 2023 OE workpaper for explicit reversal of the $31.9 million net grant benefit and related taxes; if absent, correct that year and recompute the log-trend anchor and every scenario without changing other inputs.

audit_findings.title: Safeguarding claims create an uninsured liability and franchise-risk tail outside the smooth scenarios
audit_findings.mechanism: Uninsured claims or regulatory remedies could reduce the equity bridge, while client attrition, enrollment losses, higher insurance costs or licensing restrictions could reduce OE and growth.
audit_findings.evidence: There is no assurance that our insurance, particularly coverage for sexual and physical abuse, will adequately cover our claims or damages, or continue to be readily available to us in the form or amounts we have been able to obtain in the past.
audit_findings.explanation: The U.K. review, recent safeguarding incidents and limitations on insurance coverage are disclosed, but no material claim amount, loss accrual, client attrition or enrollment impact is established. This is therefore a potentially severe forward-looking tail rather than a demonstrated numerical error in the present valuation.
audit_findings.action: Monitor the U.K. safeguarding review, asserted and unasserted claims, legal accruals, captive and external coverage limits, exclusions and deductibles, licensing remedies, insurance renewals, and post-filing client or enrollment losses; rerun downside scenarios when measurable evidence emerges.
